note: Will Anderson showed up again in Week 4, tallying three solos, two assists, 0.5 sacks, one tackle for loss, and one blocked kick. Anderson has recorded at least a half sack in every game this season and is now up to 4.5 on the season. Anderson should be contending for Defensive Player of the Year honors this season and will be a top-five option at his position regardless of opponent. Treat him as such for a tasty Week 5 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Dallas Turner stayed hot in Week 4, generating three solos, two sacks, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Turner has recorded at least a half sack in every game this season and is up to 5.5 sacks on the season, good for second in the league. The breakout is real, and it looks like Turner is ready to compete for DPoY honors now that he has a full time role. Treat the Vikings star pass rusher as a top-five option until he cools down considerably.

Byron Young went off in Week 4, racking up four solos, two assists, 2.5 sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Young has settled into life without Jared Verse, Aaron Donald, or Myles Garrett and has recorded at least one sack in two of his last three games. Up to 3.5 sacks on the season, Young will be on sack watch again for Week 5, thanks to a plus matchup against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. Tap Young as a top-five option for the plus matchup.

Darius Robinson showed up in Week 4, notching two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 31 percent of the snaps. It was the first sack of the season for Darius, who will remain a boom-or-bust DL4/5 type until he shows more consistency or earns a larger weekly snap share. Look elsewhere for your Week 5 DL3.

Josh Sweat showed up in Week 4, notching three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The sack was the first of the season for Sweat, who has been battling knee and/or groin issues for most of the season. Count Sweat as more DL4/5 than DL3 while his snap count is down around the 50 percent mark, and he continues to pop up on the injury report. Look elsewhere for your Week 5 DL3 play.

Quinnen Williams showed up in Week 4, racking up two solo, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. It was the first sack of the season for Quinnen, who has done his best to keep his fantasy value afloat with a tackle for loss or a forced fumble in each of his prior games. Williams is safe to count as a DT1 again, especially now that Dallas has taken steps to address their secondary issues. Tap Williams as a Dt1/DT3 option for Week 5.

Boye Mafe stepped up in Week 4, racking up three solos, two assists, one sack, and three tackles for loss. Mafe is leading the Bengals edge group in snaps and should be locked into a starter's role for the rest of the season. He has two sacks on the year and profiles as a boom-or-bust DL3 option. Mafe has DL2 sack upside but is not typically registering enough tackles to keep his value afloat when he doesn't get to the quarterback. Tap Mafe as a top-36 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Odafe Oweh showed up in Week 4, notching one solo, one sack, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery on 57 percent of the snaps. Oweh is up to two sacks on the season, but it is in a deep enough rotation that he is going to be more of a boom-or-bust proposition than originally anticipated. He can still be counted as a top-25 option, but expectations should be tempered as far as his weekly floor is concerned. Odafe still has double-digit sack upside, making him a top-25 option going forward.

Zach Sieiler showed up in Week 4, notching three solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss on a season high 78 percent of the snaps. Sieiler makes for a strong DT1/DL4 option now that he is back to his full complement of snaps. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals. Start him where needed.

Jermaine Johnson stepped up in Week 4, tallying two solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 48 percent of the snaps. Johnson has had a slow start to the season, with the sack being his first and being limited to two or fewer solos in each of the previous three games. Johnson is playing just around 50 percent of the snaps in the edge rotation in Tennessee and will need to start producing more to see his role expand. He has enough talent to warrant a spot on your roster, but he is nothing more than a bye week filler DL4 type until he starts to get rolling. Leave him on benches for Week 5.

Isaiah McGuire showed up again in Week 4, tallying two solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 60 percent of the snaps. McGuire has recorded a sack in two straight and is playing an expanded role due to Alex Wright being lost for the season. He will hold off Sam Williams as long as he is producing and is worth a look during the byes. Start him where needed.

Elijah Ponder was at it again in Week 4, reeling off three solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. Ponder is up to 2.5 sacks on the season, with at least a half sack in three straight games. Harold Landy is at least a few more weeks from returning, giving fantasy managers a strong DL3 option to tap during the early byes. The DL5 through four weeks of action, Ponder needs to be rostered and started everywhere until he cools down.

Josh Uche stepped up in Week 4, tallying two solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. It was the first sack of the season for the Dolphins pass rusher, who played every snap in Week 4, compared to around 50-55 percent in the first three weeks of the season. Uche will have more opportunities to produce if he keeps a starter-level snap share, something that could propel him into the weekly DL3 conversation. For now, keep him glued to benches until he shows more consistency, or we get confirmation that his weekly role has expanded permanently. Look elsewhere for Week 5.

Alim McNeill stayed hot in Week 4, racking up two solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 82 percent of the snaps. McNeill earned an expanded role in Week 4, thanks to his strong start to the season, and responded by adding another sack to his ledger. Now at three sacks on the season, he is tied for second most in the league among defensive tackles. McNeil has 22 pressures in four games, including at least six in each of his last three games. Treat McNeill as a DT1/DL3 option as long as he is cooking.

Maliek Collins stepped up in Week 4, tallying two solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss on a season high 79 percent of the snaps. It was the first sack of the season for Collins and also his first game with more than one solo. However, set to see an expanded role for at least one week with Mason Graham deemed week-to-week with MCL and ankle injuries. Collins is a potential DT2 option during the byes, including this week, thanks to a plus matchup against the New York Jets.

Tyree Wilson showed up in Week 4, racking up four solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The sack was the first of the season for Wilson, who was a health scratch just last week. Wilson actually recorded the sack when he kicked inside, so there could be a path to more snaps even when Carl Granderson and/or Anfernee Jennings are healthy. However, as it stands, his role is too tenuous, and one week of production shouldn't be enough to start him in Week 5 anyway. Stash him where feasible but look elsewhere for Week 5.

Walter Nolen was excellent in Week 4, registering three solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 61 percent of the snaps. The snap share was a season high, and Nolen responded with his first sack of the season. Nolen profiles as a future DT1 mainstay, but will need to show more consistency stopping the run or getting to the quarterback in order to boost his weekly floor. For now, stash him where possible but leave him far from fantasy lineups for Week 5.

Darius Robinson showed up in Week 4, notching two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 31 percent of the snaps. It was the first sack of the season for Darius, who will remain a boom-or-bust DL4/5 type until he shows more consistency or earns a larger w
eekly snap share. Look elsewhere for your Week 5 DL3.

Jacob Rodriguez showed out in Week 4, notching nine solos and nine assists. Rodriguez has forced his way into the LB1 mix with his stellar IDP production and should be counted as an LB1 option going forward. The LB5 through for weeks of action, Rodriguez is a must-start regardless of opponent.

Jack Campbell showed up in Week 4, reeling off six solos and eight assists. Campbell has been more inconsistent than anyone may have anticipated after his LB1-level run over the past couple of seasons, but having a competent running mate has lowered his weekly floor and, so far, his upside. Campbell is still a top-15 play, but his days of being locked in as a top-three weekly option are over, at least for now. Start Campbell as an upside top-12 option for Week 5.

Ernest Jones was excellent in Week 4, reeling off six solos, six assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, one interception, and one pass defended. Jones is locked in as a top-10 option and should be treated as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Jordyn Brooks showed up in Week 4, tallying five solos, eight assists, and one pass defended. Brooks has registered five solos in two of his four contests but looks to have lost the LB1 overall upside he showed in previous seasons with the Dolphins. Teammate Jacob Rodriguez has sapped some of his upside, but he remains a top-12 option. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Alex Singleton was at it again in Week 4, tallying seven solos, seven assists, and one tackle for loss. Singleton has recorded five or more solos in every game so far, pushing himself back into the LB1 mix in the process. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Foyesade Oluokun showed up in Week 4, racking up six solos, one assist, one forced fumble, one interception, and one pass defended. Oluokun is no longer the top-five mainstay he used to be, but outings like this remind us that the upside is still there. Tap Foye as a top-15 option for Week 5, thanks to a plus matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Tremaine Edmunds showed out in Week 4, racking up eight solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Edmunds looks to be rounding back into his former LB1 form, registering six or more solos in three of four. Edmunds can be counted as a top-15 option going forward.

Arvell Reese has been an elite IDP producer to start his NFL career, most recently tallying nine solos, one tackle for loss, one interception, and three passes defended. Reese has recorded five or more solos in three of his four contests and, thanks to back-to-back splash weeks, is the LB6. Tap Reese as an LB1 play as long as he is cooking.

Jihaad Campbell was excellent in Week 4, racking up nine solos. Jihaad has recorded five or more solos in three of his four contests, helping push him to LB11 status through four weeks of action. Tap Campbell as an LB1 option going forward, including this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Robert Spillane showed up in Week 4, tallying five solos, three assists, and one forced fumble. Spillane has recorded five or more solos in two of four games and remains locked in as a top-15 option. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Jamien Sherwood was excellent in Week 4, racking up five solos, eight assists, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. This was Sherwood's first game with five or more solos and is hopefully a sign that he is ready to move back towards being the top-15 option IDP managers hoped for. Tap Jamien as a top-25 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Demario Davis was excellent in Week 4, racking up five solos, five assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Demario has been producing at a high level and checks into Week 5 as the LB13 in total fantasy points. Treat the veteran linebacker as a top-25 option while he's cooking.

Josiah Trotter was at it again in Week 4, racking up seven solos and two assists. Trotter has been on fire to start his NFL career, checking into Week 5 as the LB13, thanks to two spike weeks and a splash week in his three games played. Trotter is the LB2 in fppg and should be counted as a top-10 option going forward. Tap Josiah as an LB1 play for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Barrett Carter showed up in Week 4, tallying five solos, six assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Barrett has been a strong LB3 play, recording two games with five solos, while managing just two solos in his other two contests. The inconsistency keeps him in the LB3 realm, but he can be counted among the elites of that tier. Tap Carter as a top-30 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Akeem Davis-Gaither was excellent in Week 4, racking up five solos and three assists. ADG has recorded five or more solos in three of his four games, solidifying the Colts linebacker as a top-20 option going forward. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Payton Wilson stayed hot in Week 4, racking up seven solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Wilson has been a consistent producer on the young season, turning in three spike weeks en route to LB17 status through four games. Wilson is safe to be counted as a top-20 option until he cools down, but the smart money is on Payton staying in the top-25 mix all season.

Devin Bush showed up in Week 4, registering two solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Bush has recorded three or fewer solos in every game this season but has managed to add a tackle for loss in three straight, keeping his fantasy value afloat. Tap Bush as a top-36 option during the byes.

Drake Thomas stayed hot in Week 4, tallying four solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, one interception, and one pass defended. The LB10 through four weeks of action, Drake can be counted as a top-15 option going forward. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Mack Wilson stepped up in Week 4, reeling off four solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Wilson has been the LB3/LB4 type most expected him to be, but has added value now that the byes are here and he just turned in his best fantasy performance of the season. Wilson should have a busy afternoon against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, giving him what should be a solid floor for the plus matchup. Tap Wilson as a top-36 option against Detroit.

T.J. Watt was at it again in Week 4, tallying four solos, one sack, two tackles for loss, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended. Watt is back to producing at a high level now that he is healthy, and he ranks third in the league with 4.5 sacks, behind only Greg Rousseau and Will Anderson. Watt has worked his way back into the weekly top-three conversation and should be treated as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Dre Greenlaw stepped up in Week 4, racking up seven solos, five assists, and one forced fumble. Greenlaw has disappointed IDP managers since returning to San Francisco, producing like more of a LB3/4 than the LB2 many had him pegged to be. His Week 4 performance was a step in the right direction, especially with the byes finally upon us. Tap Greenlaw as an upside LB3 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Jake Hansen was forced to step up in Week 4 and responded with seven solos, five assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 100 percent of the snaps. Hansen has been thrust into an expanded role since Azeez Al-Shaair suffered a groin injury in Week 3. Hansen should remain a starter after outplaying Kenneth Murray, who may miss Week 5 due to being in concussion protocol. The upside here is viewed as limited, but the spike week puts him in the mix for the byes where the options may get thin. Tap Hansen as a LB3/4 option for a tasty Week 5 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Dorian Williams showed up in Week 4, tallying four solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Williams has recorded four or more solos in every game, settling him as a top-25 option. Count him as one for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

Trenton Simpson stepped up in Week 4, tallying two solos, seven assists, one interception, and one pass defended on 56 percent of the snaps. Simpson plays what looks like a rotational role due to Baltimore making frequent use of three safety sets. Teddye Buchanan has seen his role start to grow (19 percent of the snaps in Week 4), but Simpson is going to remain the starter as long as he keeps playing well. The LB15 through four weeks of action, Simpson needs to be rostered and started in all competitive leagues as long as he is cooking.

Omar Speights showed up again in Week 4, racking up five solos and one sack on just 28 percent of the snaps. Speights saw his role dwindle against the Eagles after Saquon Barkley was lost for the game, reducing the need for the Rams to have Omar on the field, since he is usually on the field to stop the run. With that said, Speights has a sack in two straight games and becomes a bye week flex option due to his recent production. You should not want to start him in 12 team leagues, but he has been producing enough to be worth not only rostering but starting for Week 5, thanks to what should be a heavy dose of the run in Week 5 against Josh Allen, James Cook, and the Buffalo Bills.

Khalil Mack was at it again in Week 4, tallying four solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 68 percent of the snaps. Mack now has a sack in three straight games and sits at three on the season. He doesn't appear to need to worry about ceding his snap share to Akheem Mesidor, as Mack, Mesidor, and Tuli Tuipulotu are able to share the field together with Mesidor kicking inside. Mack needs to be treated as a top-25 option as long as he is producing like a DL1.

Harold Perkins stepped up on Monday Night Football, racking up seven solos, three assists, 0.5 sacks, and one pass defended. The rookie sixth-round pick has played over 65 percent of the snaps for two weeks in a row and responded with his first spike week against New Orleans. Perkins has seen his role expand to starter snap territory; that, coupled with his production, has put him on the LB3 radar for Week 5. Treat him as one for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Zaven Collins stepped up in Week 4, generating three solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. The sack was the first of the season for Collins, who has also started to make more of an impact against the run. He still doesn't play enough snaps to be fantasy relevant most weeks, managing just a 63 percent snap share in Week 4 due to a deep edge rotation in the desert. Stash him in 16+ team leagues, but look elsewhere until he starts to heat up.

Uchenna Nwosu stepped up in Week 4, notching his first sack of the season and finishing with two solos, one assist, the sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Nwosu has two spike weeks to his name, making him bench worthy, but with just one sack and a rotational role that has kept him under 52 percent of the snaps all season, he is hard to trust with just two teams on bye. Keep him stashed where needed, but look elsewhere for your Week 5 DL3.

Budda Baker has been excellent this season, most recently tabulating two solos, three assists, one interception, and two passes defended. Budda's spike week comes one week after his first splash week of the season, making it evident that Baker is currently in top-15 mode. Budda, of course, is playing either for a new contract or to force the Cardinals to keep him rostered past the start of the 2027 league year. Budda has no guaranteed money left on his deal and is playing like it. Tap Baker as a top-15 option going forward; he is going to be motivated all season.

Evan Williams has been one of the biggest surprises of the IDP season. The DB1 through four weeks of action, Williams finished Week 4 with three solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, one interception, and two passes defended. Williams has two splash weeks and two spike weeks to his name and needs to be counted as a DB1 play until he cools down. Fire him up as a top-12 option for a tasty Week 5 matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Nick Emmanwori stepped up in Week 4, posting eight solos, one assist, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Emmanwori recorded his first spike week of the season and looks like he is ready to reclaim top-five status at the position. Tap him as a top-10 play for a plus Week 5 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Jalen Pitre showed up in Week 4, registering seven solos, two assists, and one tackle for loss. Pitre has recorded four or more solos in two of his four contests, settling him in as more of a back-end DB2 than the elite option some may have hoped for. He remains a top-25 option weekly and should be treated as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Xavier Watts was at it again in Week 4, racking up five solos, three assists, and 0.5 sacks. Watts has registered three consecutive spike weeks, locking him as a top-20 option until he cools down. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the banged-up Baltimore Ravens.

Cooper DeJean stepped up in Week 4, racking up three solos, two assists, one interception, and two passes defended. It was the first spike week for Cooper, who has topped three solo tackles just once all season. Drop DeJean down to the low-end DB3/CB2 realm until he starts to show some consistency. We all know the talent and upside is there, so he remains a DB3 option, but lower your expectations until he starts producing at a level commensurate with the DB2 he was expected to be.

Kamari Lassiter was at it again in Week 4, notching seven solos, one assist, and two passes defended. Kamari has posted back-to-back spike weeks, solidifying him as a top-30 option. The DB16 in total fantasy points, Lassiter is a corner who is fed a steady diet of tackle production due to playing across from Derek Stingley Jr. Tap Kamari as a DB3 with DB2 upside for Week 5 and beyond.

Christian Izien was excellent in Week 4, racking up seven solos, four assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Izien looked like an elite IDP force in his two starts, posting two splash weeks. The splash weeks put him as the DB1 in fantasy points per game and the DB15 in overall fantasy points despite making just two starts since being called up from the practice squad in Week 2 (he played five percent of the snaps against Buffalo that week). Izien could have one more start in him, but Brian Branch has returned to limited sessions for the Detroit Lions. He is expected to see his snaps managed if he suits up this weekend, but Izien will likely be the one leaving the field when Branch takes his snaps. And if Branch is deemed healthy enough to play, you have to imagine that he would be ready for at least a 50 percent snap share, or the Lions would probably just choose to sit him out another week. Izien is a start if Branch is ruled out by Friday, but should remain on fantasy benches if Branch is active.

Devon Witherspoon showed up in Week 4, tallying eight solos, one assist, and one tackle for loss. It was the first spike week for Witherspoon, who had been right on the cusp in two of his previous three weeks. Devon has established himself as a locked-in CB1/DB3 play due to his tackle production. The Seahawks corner has registered four or more solos in three straight games. Tap Witherspoon as a top-36 DB option for a tasty Week 5 matchup against the banged-up San Francisco 49ers.

Minkah returned with a bang in Week 4, tallying eight solos, eight assists, one interception, and one pass defended. He played 100 percent of the snaps in his first game back from a groin injury, and his performance suggests that he is safe to be counted as a top-15 option immediately. Dane Belton took the snap hit with Fitzpatrick returning. Tap Fitzpatrick as a DB1 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Dane Belton showed up in Week 4, recording six solos, eight assists, and one pass defended. It was the first spike week for Belton, who has been solid for fantasy managers, registering four or more solos in three straight contests. Tap Belton as a top-30 type as long as he is starting and producing.

Grant Delpit showed up in Week 4, racking up four solos, two assists,  one interception, and one pass defended. Delpit has been inconsistent but has two spike weeks to his name in four weeks of action, keeping him in the mix as an upside DB3 play. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the New York Jets.

Reed Blankenship was excellent in Week 4, generating five solos and six assists. Reed has recorded five or more solos in two straight games and checks into Week 5 as the DB18, thanks to back-to-back spike weeks. Count Blankenship as a top-25 option as long as he is producing.

Amik Robertson was excellent in Week 4, racking up seven solos, two assists, and one pass defended. The DB8/CB2 through four weeks of action, Robertson is a must-start DB3/CB1 play as long as he stays hot. Amik has posted three straight 'spike' weeks with four or more solos in each. Count him as a top-36 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the New York Giants.

C.J. Henderson went off again in Week 4, exploding with nine solos, one assist, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended. The former first-round pick has looked like just that since stepping in for the injured AJ Terrell and likely made himself quite a bit of money with his dominant two-game stretch. He is hard to project for IDP, but he is too hot to ignore while he is sizzling. Fresh off an eight solo, three passes defended Week 3, Henderson should be tapped as a flex option while he is producing at an elite level. Act accordingly for Week 5.

Justin Walley stayed liquid in Week 4, racking up five solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Walley has already recorded two games with five solos, offering fantasy managers steady tackle production with a pass defended usually in the offing as well. Tap Walley as a CB1 option while he is cooking, with an eye on potentially utilizing the slot corner as a DB3 option as we get deeper into the byes.

Jacob Parrish stepped up in Week 4, tallying five solos, one tackle for loss, one interception, and two passes defended. Parrish has registered back-to-back games with four or more solos, putting him squarely in the CB2 mix. Parrish is not someone those in 12-team leagues without dedicated CB slots should be paying much attention to. Add him to watch lists but look elsewhere for Week 5.

Jourdan Lewis showed up in Week 4, racking up three solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Lewis has recorded two spike weeks so far but remains more of a CB league option, at least for now. He is an easy CB1 play but remains more DB4/flex than DB3, at least for now. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup.

Jarrian Jones was at it again in Week 4, generating seven solos, one tackle for loss, and three passes defended. Jarrian has now posted back-to-back spike weeks, forcing his way into the CB2 discussion in the process. Jones has seen over 70 percent of the snaps over the last three weeks, and while he is currently better known for his violent facemask on Ja'Marr Chase, he is a burgeoning IDP asset in CB leagues who belongs on deeper DB league radars as well. Treat him as a top-25 CB option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Deonte Banks returned to action with a bang for the New York Giants, recording one solo, three assists, one interception, four passes defended, and one touchdown. Banks has been impressive in his two starts this season and belongs on the CB2 radar. He will need to show some more consistency before we can start trusting him as a DB3 or CB1 option, but he has certainly flashed the upside to project his inclusion in that conversation in the near future. For now, though, keep counting him as a CB2/DB5 and look elsewhere for your Week 5 DB3.

Rayuan Lane stepped up in Week 4, tallying six solos, two assists, and one pass defended on 57 percent of the snaps. Lane saw an expanded role with both Eric Murray and Caleb Ransaw going down with injuries and responded with a DB2-level fantasy outing and a key stop on Chase Brown. Lane is a Week 5 option with Murray ultimately expected to be ruled out for the Jaguars' annual London game. Keep him on the radar as a potential DB3/flex option.
